name: wren-cli
desc: Simple REPL and CLI tool for running Wren scripts
why: Wren is a small, elegant embeddable scripting language, and its CLI is a clean entry point into a lesser-known language.

brief.what_it_is: wren-cli is a standalone command-line tool for running Wren scripts, with an interactive REPL as well as file execution. Its input is Wren source code, either typed at the REPL or given as script files, and its output is whatever those scripts produce. Beyond running the language, it adds its own standard library and modules for operating-system work such as file IO and networking, so it works as a general-purpose single-binary scripting tool. The README describes it as a small and simple tool and says it is a work in progress. The binary is named wren_cli.
brief.why_it_exists: Wren is intentionally minimal and has no built-in file, network, or other IO, so a separate host tool is needed to give scripts access to those things. The docs give the framing as 'It's fun to make things', 'It's always a good idea to test the language you're making!', and that interest was expressed in a scriptable tool using Wren.
brief.how_it_works: The CLI embeds the Wren VM and uses libuv to implement its IO functionality. It is its own project, not bundled with the Wren language, and it exposes its own standard library and modules on top of the VM. The README does not describe the REPL internals or the module API in detail.

commands_seen.context: macOS: move into the make project folder before building.
macOS and Linux: build the CLI from inside the make project folder (projects/make.mac or projects/make).
Linux: move into the make project folder before building.
FreeBSD: move into the BSD make project folder before building.
FreeBSD: the build command used in place of make inside projects/make.bsd.
Alternative build: generate a Visual Studio 2019 project for Windows using premake; the README gives this as an example of the --os flag, run from Linux.

brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond the build. Build from source: on Windows, open the Visual Studio projects in projects/vs20xx; on macOS, use the Xcode project in projects/xcode or run make in projects/make.mac; on Linux, run make in projects/make; on FreeBSD, run gmake in projects/make.bsd. Other project files can be generated with premake, found in projects/premake, where the README says premake5 alpha 14 was used. The README does not mention Homebrew, and the brew formula's caveats were empty. No accounts or runtimes are needed beyond a C toolchain and libuv, which I infer from the README but which the README does not list explicitly. No first-run steps are documented in what I read.
brief.standout: The CLI is a clean, real-world example of embedding a small scripting language with a host that supplies its own IO through libuv. It is a useful reference for anyone curious how an embeddable VM gets files and networking.
brief.status: Unknown. The README has a Travis CI build badge pointing at the main branch, but I found no release date, last commit date, or maintenance note in the README or the docs page. The docs describe it as a work in progress, and the README still refers to alpha 14 of premake and Travis CI, which suggests it may not have been touched in a while, but I could not confirm that.
brief.caveats: The README calls it a work in progress and only documents building from source; there is no install or usage section beyond a pointer to wren.io/cli. Build paths differ per platform, and the Windows section just points at Visual Studio folders with no commands. The docs page lists a 'Wren CLI' feature set but gives no specific command-line usage. The license was not visible in what I read. The homepage's 'Build Status' badge is for Travis CI, which may no longer be in use. The brew formula's caveats were empty.
quotes: The CLI project is a small and simple REPL and CLI tool for running Wren scripts.
It is backed by libuv to implement IO functionality, and is a work in progress.
Wren as a language is intentionally designed to be minimal.
